findings.title: fetch_error_details misaligns error IDs with nodestore results via zip on dict values
findings.body: In fetch_error_details, `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id, and the code builds ErrorEvent objects with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Dict values are not guaranteed to be in the same order as the requested node ids, and any node that is missing (deleted/expired event) is simply absent from the dict, which shifts every subsequent pairing. The result is that error titles, messages, and timestamps can be attributed to the wrong event id (the `id` field of ErrorEvent), and the filtering `if data is not None` does not fix the offset. The code should look up each event by its node id (e.g. `events.get(node_id)`) instead of zipping positional lists.

findings.title: Error event timestamps read from nodestore are ISO strings, causing TypeError when compared with float breadcrumb timestamps
findings.body: fetch_error_details builds ErrorEvent objects with `timestamp=data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` from raw nodestore event data. Nodestore event payloads store `timestamp` as an ISO-8601 string (and the 0.0 fallback is a float), while breadcrumb events from replay segments carry float timestamps. Downstream, `get_request_data` sorts error_events by timestamp (`error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"])`) and `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`, which mixes str and float operands and raises TypeError in Python 3 (both in the sort when a defaulted 0.0 is present, and in every comparison against a float breadcrumb timestamp). This will make the summarize-breadcrumbs endpoint raise a 500 for any replay that has associated error events. Timestamps should be parsed to floats (e.g. via `datetime.fromisoformat` / `Event.timestamp`) before use.

findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget renders an empty table, discarding the actual query results
findings.body: In tableResultComponent, when `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` and completely ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, `loading`, and `fieldAliases` that the non-flagged `StyledSimpleTableChart` branch uses. Any organization with the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag enabled will see empty dashboard table widgets (no headers, no rows) regardless of the underlying data. Either the flag branch should be removed until real data wiring is implemented, or the actual result data should be passed to TableWidgetVisualization.

findings.title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template references PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration
findings.body: The new helpers `_truncate_title`, `get_environment_info`, and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` were all added to the `CommitContextIntegration` class (the diff hunk places them at the end of that class, immediately before `class OpenPRCommentWorkflow`). However, `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, and the GitHub/GitLab integration subclasses call `self.get_environment_info(issue)` and `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` from within `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`/`GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` (which derive from `PRCommentWorkflow`, the OpenPRCommentWorkflow-based class, not from CommitContextIntegration). Unless PRCommentWorkflow also inherits from CommitContextIntegration, these lookups raise AttributeError whenever a merged-PR suspect-issue comment is generated, breaking the PR comment workflow. The helpers should live on (or be reached through) the workflow class, e.g. via `self.integration._truncate_title(...)`.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check and request validation
findings.body: The `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` analytics event is recorded at the top of `post()`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check (which returns 404) and before `validate_preprod_artifact_schema` (which returns 400). This means the event fires for every request to the endpoint, including requests from organizations without the feature and requests with malformed bodies that never reach assembly. The analytics data will overcount usage and include unauthenticated-shape/invalid traffic, defeating its purpose as a usage metric. Record the event after the feature gate and schema validation succeed.

findings.title: Mutual-exclusion validation of age/timestamp uses truthiness, so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypasses it
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` rejects the report when `self.initial_data.get("age")` is truthy, and `validate_age` rejects when `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` is truthy. Per the Reporting API, `age` is a millisecond count that can legitimately be 0 (report generated immediately), and timestamp 0 is permitted by the field's `min_value=0`. When age=0 and a timestamp is also present (or vice versa), the falsy check passes and the report is accepted with both fields, violating the intended either-or invariant between the Working Draft and Editor's Draft formats. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` instead of truthiness.

findings.title: query() mutates the caller's selected_columns list in place
findings.body: In `ourlogs.query`, when orderby is `[-timestamp]` or `[timestamp]`, the function appends `tags[sentry.timestamp_precise,number]` to `selected_columns` directly. This mutates the list passed in by the caller, so the hidden tie-breaking column leaks into any downstream use of that same list (response meta/fields, caching of the field list, or repeated calls that would append the column again on the same list). Build a new list (e.g. `selected_columns = [*selected_columns, precise_timestamp]`) instead of appending to the input parameter.

findings.title: Failed feedback summaries render as an empty summary panel instead of being hidden
findings.body: `tooFewFeedbacks` is computed as `data.numFeedbacksUsed === 0 && !data.success`, so when the summary generation fails with feedbacks present (numFeedbacksUsed > 0, success: false, summary: null), the hook reports tooFewFeedbacks=false and isError=false. FeedbackSummary then falls through to rendering the 'Feedback Summary' box with `summary` of null, showing users a permanently empty summary card rather than hiding it or surfacing an error state. The success/failure distinction should be based on `data.success` (or the summary being non-null), not just on the feedback count.
